minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to seek care of part of the Pleasant Street lot and set new officers; dog policy held for a draft.
minutes.summary: The commission reorganized, with Chris Sullivan as vice chair, Karen as chair and Susannah Jewel as secretary. It recommended accepting donated bleachers at McNally Field and voted to tell the Open Space Committee it wants part of the Pleasant Street property. Members also discussed Marshall Park parking, Marshall Pond light posts and invasives, the Marshall Park survey results, leashed dogs in parks, and cash payment at the town beach.

budget_items.what_was_said: A funding source tentatively agreed could be used toward replacing the bathrooms, with options to be presented by June.
Money for the consultant becomes available July 1, and a bid or RFP process needs to start now.
A donated picnic table might need to be ADA compliant; it was suggested DPW could cover it under care and maintenance, as with earlier year-end money for lifeguard seats.
Chair wants regular financial updates on the park budget, including money for field care and maintenance, put on a future agenda.
A member suggested grants for ADA-accessible features could reduce the financial burden on the town.
A prior program charged a small fee per participant.
The commission must accept cash for beach passes under state law, with deposits handled through the DPW and the treasurer's office.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to tell the Open Space Committee it wants ownership of at least part of the Pleasant Street property.
It voted to recommend accepting donated bleachers for McNally Field, which go to the Select Board for final approval.
The commission reorganized, voting in a vice chair, a chair and a secretary.
It voted to ask the DPW how to remove two light posts at Marshall Pond.
A dog policy for leashed dogs in parks was held; a member is to research other towns and draft wording.

why_it_matters: Ownership of the Pleasant Street land would decide whether part of it becomes park land run by this commission, so residents may later be asked to weigh in or vote on it.
Money for a Marshall Park planning consultant becomes available July 1, so the park's future design and cost depend on a bid process that has to start now.
A leashed-dog rule would apply in town parks, and the town beach must accept cash for passes under state law.
watch_next: Next meeting on Wednesday June 30, likely in person, where options for funding the bathroom replacement are due.
The Select Board's final approval of the McNally Field bleachers gift, and a draft dog policy.
